content.text:
Checkout deploy `ccf7a0f` (14:46:05) lines up with the spike. Checkout p99 went from about 70 ms at 14:45 to 3006 ms at 14:46 and stayed at 3–4.3 s through 14:59. The earlier inventory (12:20) and cart (14:18) deploys come well before the jump.

The diff, labelled a readability refactor, replaces the single batched `order_items WHERE order_id IN (...)` query with one query per open order inside a loop. That is an N+1 pattern.

The log agrees. There are 201 batched `IN (?)` queries before the deploy and 1555 per-order `order_id = ?` queries after it.

Rolling back `ccf7a0f`, or restoring the batched fetch, should fix it. I didn't check `db_pool_utilization`, so I can't say whether the extra queries also saturated the DB pool.

**Root cause:** `ccf7a0f` — the "readability" refactor of `CheckoutSummaryHandler.build_summary` replaced the single batched `order_items IN (...)` query with one query per open order, an N+1 pattern that multiplies DB round-trips per checkout request and pushed p99 from ~70 ms to 3–4 s.
